statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 22% as NQ futures extend their retracement to roughly 120 points off the 30,370.00 session low while the 2-year yield falls 4bp to 4.87% and the 10-year adds only about 1bp.
recommendation: Tail sits two points below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH rather than BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The reading reflects three amplifiers that have stopped extending: the front end has turned lower, the 10-year is adding roughly a basis point against far larger prior daily moves, and VIX has come off its session high. Price has also rewarded a retracement rather than holding a fresh extreme. Brent above $100 on the Strait of Hormuz navigation threat is the one amplifier still extending, and it keeps Stress elevated. The evidence-based danger window is narrowed to 12:30-15:00 UTC, spanning the claims release, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the early-afternoon data. Observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published; an orderly two-way open would argue for a lower one.
headline: NQ extends its bounce off the 30,370.00 low as the 2-year eases and the 10-year move flattens
body: NQ futures trade near 30,490, down about 0.9% from the 30,764.75 previous close, with the session low unchanged at 30,370.00. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and on that low. The single most important change since the previous hour is that the retracement off it has extended rather than failed: price is now roughly 120 points above the low, against about 60 points an hour ago. That is the specific behaviour the block-band readings published at 09:00 and 13:00 UTC yesterday were pricing against, and it is the reason Tail eases rather than pushing back into the block band. The macro driver is unchanged and remains duration rather than anything equity-specific. The US 10-year holds about 5.13%, its highest since July 2007, after a weak five-year auction and S&P Global composite PMI at 58.4 against a 55.3 consensus, and the 30-year is near its highest since 2004. Two qualifications matter. First, the 10-year is adding only about one basis point today against far larger moves earlier in the week, so the repricing is decelerating at the long end. Second, the 2-year has eased 4bp to 4.87%, so the front end is now moving against the hawkish impulse even though futures still price roughly a 71% chance of an October increase and above 58% for December. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said yesterday that further policy adjustments are likely to be needed, which is the commentary that drove that repricing. Volatility is the second de-escalating input: VIX trades at 16.16 against a 15.18 close, up 6.45%, but below its 16.57 session high and still a low absolute level for a multi-decade-high yield backdrop. Energy is the exception and the main reason Stress stays elevated. Brent is at $104.83, up 1.70%, and WTI at $93.06, up 0.98%, after Iranian statements that navigation through the Strait of Hormuz would be restricted while sanctions remain and that the conflict could widen beyond the Gulf. US and Iranian leaders exchanged barbs at the UN General Assembly, so the escalation channel is open and unresolved. Japanese government bonds add to the Stress backdrop, with the 10-year JGB at a 30-year high of 3.06% and the yen near 157.9. Premarket megacap tone is soft but not disorderly, with Meta down about 2% and Nvidia about 1%. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed yesterday at 30,470.29, down 0.85%, inside a 30,353.88-30,706.23 range and above its low, so retracement was still being rewarded at the last cash close. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run but was collected at 06:48 UTC, making it roughly 287 minutes old, and was marked partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable. Under the supporting-evidence contract it is stale, so no part of it was used as evidence and every figure above comes from independent current sources. The structural checkpoints ahead are the 12:00 UTC Barkin speech, jobless claims at 12:30 UTC against a 201K consensus, Hammack at 12:50 UTC, the 13:30 UTC US cash open, new home sales at 14:00 UTC and the Kansas City Fed index at 15:00 UTC.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 12-15% through the European and early US hours of Sep 23 in a normal-to-mixed regime, printed 25% for the 14:00 UTC hour as the post-PMI bond leg developed, then held 20-24% through the US afternoon and the Asian session. It eased to 17-19% between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC, printed 22% at 04:00 UTC on a brief trend-down read, and reached 24% and 25% for the 08:00 and 09:00 UTC hours as the duration move re-accelerated into a fresh session low, before easing to 24% for the 10:00 UTC slot as the first retracement off that low appeared. Stress was the more persistent signal, rising from the mid-30s to 57% at 18:00 UTC, easing to around 50% overnight and returning to 56-58% for the final three slots. Confidence held in the 84-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path holds Tail at 22-23% in the watch band through the European afternoon and the 12:30 UTC claims block, steps into the block band at 25% for the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours covering the cash open and the first full cash hour, and returns to the watch band at 21-23% from 15:00 UTC. That two-hour step defines the evidence-based danger window, narrowed to 12:30-15:00 UTC. Tail then decays through the US afternoon and evening to 16-18% across the Asian session and drifts back to 18-19% across the following European hours as the amplifier stack is assumed to unwind slowly. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, peaking at 60%, because 10-year yields at a July 2007 high, the 10-year JGB at a 30-year high and Brent above $100 persist regardless of intraday structure. Confidence decays from 86% to 64% as the current price-path evidence ages across the window. The path assumes the rate-repricing regime stays unresolved but that price discovery remains orderly and retracements continue to be rewarded. Observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published, while a further easing of the front end or a genuine two-way cash open would argue for a lower one.
